raw_segments.text: Not with pleasure, though I was bound to him by so many ties, no, with considerable disturbance,
some mortification, and a keen sense of incongruity.
If I could have kept him away by paying money, I certainly would have paid money.
My greatest reassurance was that he was coming to Barnards Inn, not to Hammersmith, and consequently
would not fall in Bentley Drummel's way.
I had little objection to his being seen by Herbert or his father, for both of whom I
had a respect, but I had the sharpest sensitiveness as to his being seen by Drummel, whom I held
So, throughout life, our worst weaknesses and meannesses are usually committed for the
sake of the people whom we most despise.
